title: Proof-of-principle Long-distance Sagnac Twin-field Quantum Key Distribution Network
authors: Reem Mandil, Yen-An Shih, Abhay Verma, Li Qian, Hoi-Kwong Lo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twin-field (TF) quantum key distribution (QKD) offers a promising approach to long-distance QKD networks due to its superior performance over large channel losses. Due to specialized hardware requirements, nearly all long-distance TFQKD demonstrations have only two users exchanging keys, rather than a network with three or more users. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate a proof-of-principle three-user-pair Sagnac TFQKD network spanning 127-km using single-photon avalanche detectors without any active phase stabilization or postcompensation. A secure key rate of [MATH] bits per pulse is achieved over an asymmetric communication channel with 102-km fiber and 45-dB overall loss. To our knowledge, this is the first TFQKD network without active phase stabilization or postcompensation achieved over long fibers. Our results represent a highly practical and cost-effective approach to long-distance QKD networks.

title: Towards Minimal Conditions For Ergotropy Injection In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Deependra Singh, Debarupa Saha, Ujjwal Sen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactions between a quantum system and its environment can inject ergotropy into the system, raising the question of the minimal dimensionality and physical resources required for such injection. We first show that ergotropy injection is impossible under thermal operations when both the system and environment are qubits, whereas it becomes possible when the environment is enlarged to a qutrit. We further show that already in the qubit-qubit setting, relaxing environmental thermality and allowing interactions between system and environment allows ergotropy increment under energy-conserving unitaries. To elucidate the role of interactions, we consider a two-qubit isotropic XY interaction Hamiltonian and identify its distinct degeneracy regimes. We show that, in the central-block regime, when both the initial system and environmental states are incoherent, no ergotropic gain is possible when the environment is initially thermal, irrespective of the interaction strength. In contrast, environmental athermality in the form of population inversion, while retaining incoherence, enables ergotropic injection. We derive the optimal ergotropic gain and show that environmental coherence can enhance it, while system coherence alone need not be beneficial and can even reduce the gain. We further consider the double-degenerate regime, characterized by a finite interaction strength, and demonstrate positive ergotropic gain even for a thermal environment.

motivation: Understanding the minimal resources required for ergotropy injection is key to quantum thermodynamics and work extraction from quantum systems.
method: They analyze thermal operations and energy-conserving unitaries, including a two-qubit isotropic XY interaction, examining degeneracy regimes to determine conditions for ergotropic gain.
result: Ergotropy injection is impossible for qubit-qubit under thermal operations but possible with a qutrit environment; in qubit-qubit with energy-conserving unitaries, athermal environments allow gain, and environmental coherence enhances it while system coherence may not help.
conclusion: The work clarifies fundamental limitations and requirements for ergotropy injection, highlighting the roles of environmental dimension and athermality.

title: Strong-Drive Limits In Josephson Circuits: From Chaos To An Unbound-Resonance Threshold
authors: Xinyuan You, Aniket Maiti, Yao Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong microwave drives enable fast measurement and parametric control in superconducting circuits but can induce transitions out of the intended low-energy manifold. We develop a unified description of strong-drive limits in flux- and charge-driven Josephson circuits across drive frequency and dc flux bias. Using classical phase-space analysis and Floquet--Markov simulations, we identify distinct low- and high-frequency mechanisms. At low frequency, we characterize bound-state resonances and separatrix chaos and find that the flux-drive chaos threshold depends strongly on dc flux bias. At high frequency, these mechanisms are suppressed, and the dissipative steady state transfers from the central bound-state sector to outer resonances formed by above-barrier running trajectories. The resulting unbound-resonance threshold is nearly independent of drive frequency and circuit parameters over the regime studied and is controlled primarily by dc flux bias. Coherent simulations show that parametric operation persists beyond this threshold, but at a reduced rate, setting an effective upper bound on the achievable operation speed. We derive analytical criteria for both thresholds, validate them numerically, and experimentally confirm the predicted dc-bias dependence of the low-frequency threshold in a flux-driven SQUID. We also determine the timescales for transfer into the unbound-resonance regime and relaxation back to the bound-state manifold after the drive is removed. Finally, we relate the stability limits to a complementary picture based on the junction critical current and extend the framework to multitone drives and inductively shunted circuits. Together, these results identify the mechanisms limiting strong driving and suggest routes to extend the stable operating range of Josephson circuits.

motivation: Strong microwave drives enable fast measurement and parametric control in superconducting circuits but can induce transitions out of the intended low-energy manifold, limiting performance.
method: The authors combine classical phase-space analysis, Floquet-Markov simulations, and experimental validation in a flux-driven SQUID to characterize low- and high-frequency drive mechanisms.
result: They find distinct mechanisms for low-frequency (bound-state resonances, separatrix chaos) and high-frequency (above-barrier running trajectories) regimes, with an unbound-resonance threshold nearly independent of drive frequency and controlled by dc flux bias.
conclusion: Analytical criteria for the thresholds are derived and validated, and the framework is extended to multitone drives and inductively shunted circuits, providing routes to extend stable operating range.

title: One Bit Of Collective Information Is Worth N Ln 2 Bits Of Local Information In A Many-Body Quantum Battery
authors: Akoramurthy B, Surendiran B, Xiaochun Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charging a quantum battery through a collective non-adiabatic stroke stores energy in a shared bosonic mode, but part remains locked in correlations with the collective spin and is inaccessible to cyclic unitaries acting on the mode alone. A demon holding one bit can unlock this energy, quantified by the daemonic ergotropy. We investigate the value of one bit and its dependence on where the information is obtained. Two protocols are compared at matched stored energy and matched information, using balanced two-outcome measurements carrying exactly one bit. We find that one bit about the collective coordinate unlocks N ln(2) times as much work as one bit about a single ion. For three stored-energy settings and N = 4-24, the measured scaling exponent is 0.990 +/- 0.043, while double extrapolation gives a prefactor of 0.69298 +/- 0.00044, within 0.02% of ln(2). To leading order, the daemonic gain equals nu mu^2 times the between-outcome variance of Jx, verified numerically to 1.3%. A balanced single-ion measurement resolves 1/4 of this variance, whereas a balanced collective split resolves (ln(2)/4)N. The microscopic origin of the prefactor remains open; a Gaussian median-split estimate of 1/(2pi) is excluded by 9%. One bit recovers a constant fraction of the locked energy independent of N and yields roughly twice as much work per bit as a complete readout, indicating strong diminishing returns. We also show that unnormalized gain comparisons can reverse the conclusion and that the break-even ion number does not collapse onto the Dicke superradiant threshold when the mode frequency is varied.

motivation: The goal is to quantify the value of different types of information for extracting locked energy from quantum batteries, comparing collective and local measurements.
method: Two balanced two-outcome measurement protocols (collective split and single-ion) are compared at matched stored energy via daemonic ergotropy, analyzing the scaling of work gain with system size N.
result: Collective information yields N ln(2) times the work of local information, with measured scaling exponent 0.990 and prefactor within 0.02% of ln(2); the gain is proportional to the variance of Jx.
conclusion: A single bit of collective information recovers a constant fraction of locked energy independent of N, and provides about twice as much work per bit as complete readout, highlighting diminishing returns.

title: Ancilla Mediated Steady-state Engineering In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Soham Pal, Karen Hovhannisyan, Omri Porat, Shovan Dutta, Janet Anders, Helena Knowles
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Engineering the properties of a reservoir and its coupling to a quantum system is a powerful tool for simulating quantum thermodynamic processes and for generating otherwise inaccessible steady states. title: Dprq: A Dynamic Programming-based Qubit Routing Algorithm For Collective Communication In Distributed Quantum Computing
authors: Dhaval Vaidya (north Carolina State University, Raleigh, NC, USA), Ruozhou Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed quantum computing (DQC) offers a promising approach to scale quantum computing by overcoming the resource limitations of a single quantum processor. title: Neural Networks Learn To Reconstruct Multipartite Entanglement From Quantum Marginals
authors: Matreyee Kandpal, Arvind, Kavita Dorai
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Different sets of local correlations are not equivalent: some fragments of reduced data uniquely determine a global quantum state, while others leave it ambiguous. The quantum marginal problem asks whether a collection of reduced density matrices uniquely determines a compatible global quantum state. Although generic quantum states are uniquely specified by suitable sets of marginals, different collections of marginals are not equally informative: some uniquely determine the global state, whereas others leave it ambiguous. Identifying when uniqueness holds, and reconstructing the global state from partial information, remains computationally demanding and experimentally challenging. We show that information about the multipartite entanglement class and reconstructability in four-qubit systems is compactly encoded in small sets of two- and three-qubit marginals. Using semidefinite programming, we chart the reconstructability landscape across 49 inequivalent SLOCC entanglement classes and show that uniqueness strongly depends on both entanglement structure and marginal order. Neural networks trained only on reduced density matrices learn this structure directly. They accurately classify marginal reconstructability and, when uniqueness holds, reconstruct the full four-qubit density matrix with high fidelity from two- and three-qubit marginals. We benchmark the approach on a four-qubit nuclear magnetic resonance quantum processor and demonstrate that reconstructions from experimentally measured marginals remain faithful despite phase damping and control imperfections. Our results show that neural networks can learn when local correlations uniquely specify a global quantum state, and reveal how global quantum structure is encoded in reduced data.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Law Governing Stochastic Pendulum Clocks

abstract: ArXiv:2609.04957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clocks' performance, especially their precision, is fundamentally limited by thermodynamic laws as they are physical devices. Our framework reveals a universal thermodynamic principle governing stochastic pendulum clocks beyond the conventional TUR and provides a foundation for designing optimal pendulum clocks that operate efficiently in stochastic environments.

title: Three-Photon And Hybrid Coherent-Fock Interference In A Two-Phase Six-Port Mach-Zehnder Interferometer

title: Efficient Quantum Error Correction From Three Dimensional Qubit Control

abstract: ArXiv:2609.04459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes can substantially reduce qubit overhead relative to surface codes, but their advantage depends on efficiently realizing nonlocal syndrome extraction. title: Finite-Corner Reconstruction And Separation For Cones Of Normal Maps

abstract: ArXiv:2609.04889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a finite-corner framework for convex cones of normal maps between \(\mathcal B(\mathcal H)\) and \(\mathcal B(\mathcal K)\). title: A Sim-to-Real Study Of Surface-Code Decoder Benchmarking
authors: Shay J. Manor, Leila S. Erhili, Yassine Jebbouri
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum error-correction decoders are typically benchmarked against synthetic circuit-level noise, under the assumption that a decoder's ranking under such noise transfers to hardware and improves as the noise model becomes more realistic. The Willow processor, the first to operate below the surface-code threshold, allows us to test this assumption. Rank agreement with hardware appears once the noise model gives each operation type its own error rate. Calibrating the model to the device improves absolute error rates but not rank agreement. We additionally provide the first independent evaluation of NVIDIA's Ising pre-decoder on hardware, at code distances below its training receptive field and via a mapping onto the lattice on which it was trained. Under these conditions, it holds no accuracy-latency advantage: another panel decoder matches or improves on it in both per-cycle error rate and decode latency in 278 of the 280 evaluations. We release the full pipeline and the per-shot outcome of every evaluation, so future decoders and devices can be compared.

title: Reply To The Comment On "The Axiom Of Choice And The No-Signalling Principle"
authors: \"amin Baumeler, Borivoje Daki\'c, Flavio Del Santo, Milo\v{s} Milovanovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We clarify the meaning of a probabilistic no-signalling strategy in Ref [Proc. R. Soc. A 481, 20240601]. For every fixed input, the deterministic strategy constructed using the Axiom of Choice can indeed be represented by a Dirac probability distribution over the outputs. The relevant distinction arises when one considers the complete process from input to output, with the input itself sampled according to a probability distribution. In this case, the input and output spaces must be measurable and the dependence of the conditional output distribution on the input must also be measurable. Equivalently, the conditional distributions must form a Markov kernel. The Axiom-of-Choice strategy fails precisely this measurability requirement.

result: The reply demonstrates that the proposed deterministic strategy does not satisfy the necessary measurability for a full probabilistic no-signalling process, reinforcing the importance of such conditions in quantum information theory.

title: State-Based Quantum Operations: Chameleon Gates
authors: A. T. Rezakhani S. Alipour
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce chameleon gates as a natural generalization of conventional quantum controlled-gates. Chameleon gates are state-based quantum controlled-operations that retain standard elements such as control and target systems, while introducing a new feature: the quantum knob. This knob is a quantum signal (state) that determines the operation performed by the gate. Consequently, the action and form of a chameleon gate depend dynamically on the quantum knob, allowing the gate to adapt its operation and implement transformations that are not necessarily unitary. We then employ chameleon gates as a useful building block within the recently proposed state-based quantum computation (SBQC) framework. Using this approach, we demonstrate the simulation of state-dependent (nonlinear) quantum evolutions.

title: Nitrogen Vacancy Centers In Diamond For Quantum Biosensing: Magnetometry Techniques, Platforms And Applications
authors: Sirsendu Ghosal, Umakant Prajapati, Sachin Negi, Saifian Farooq Bhat, Thejas B, Vibhav Bharadwaj
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum sensing using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond has emerged as a powerful platform for detecting ultra-low magnetic fields under ambient conditions. Owing to their long spin coherence times, optical addressability, and compatibility with aqueous environments, it has found widespread applications in biosensing and bio-imaging. This review presents the fundamental principles and recent advances in NV-based quantum magnetometry for biosensing applications, with a particular focus on measurements in aqueous medium and at cellular and molecular length scales. We discuss the underlying spin physics of NV centers and highlight two primary detection modalities: optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) and T1 relaxometry-based sensing and how these approaches aids in the detection of both static magnetic fields and dynamic magnetic noise arising from biological processes. The review explores key application areas, including nanoscale nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), monitoring of neural activity, detection of abnormal or rogue cells using NV-based platforms etc. In addition, strategies for enhancing sensitivity, such as surface functionalization of nanodiamonds, femtosecond (fs) laser-written photonic structures, and integration with microfluidic and lab-on-chip systems have also been discussed in depth. We also address the critical challenges, including surface-induced decoherence, charge-state instability, and signal-to-noise limitations in biofluids associated with NV-based biosensing applications. Finally, we outline future prospects, highlighting how NV-based magnetic biosensing provides a promising pathway for translating quantum sensing technologies into practical biomedical applications.
tldr: A review of NV center-based quantum magnetometry for biosensing, covering techniques, platforms, and applications.
motivation: To provide an overview of NV-based quantum sensing for detecting low magnetic fields in biological environments.
method: Discusses spin physics, ODMR and T1 relaxometry, and strategies to improve sensitivity such as surface functionalization and microfluidic integration.
result: Highlights key applications including nanoscale NMR, neural activity monitoring, and detection of abnormal cells.
conclusion: NV-based magnetic biosensing shows promise for practical biomedical applications.

title: QMClaw: A Scalable General-purpose Framework For Quantum Measurement And Control
authors: Zhiqiang Fan, Haoran He, Ping Lv, Junchao Wang, Yaqiang Sun, Chenhui Wang, Hanshi Zhao, Geyuyan Ma, Haoran Yang, Pengyu Han, Xiangdong Meng, Lixin Wang, Feng Yue, Weilong Wang, Zheng Shan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As quantum computing continues to scale, quantum measurement and control (QMC) are increasingly constrained by calibration workflow complexity and by requirements for low-latency execution, robust exception handling, and traceable workflow governance. Existing frameworks for QMC are specialized and task-specific, while language-model-based agents for QMC suffer from excessive latency and cannot satisfy the strict timing and control-density demands of large-scale quantum systems. Here we propose QMClaw, a general, workflow-oriented framework for QMC built, featuring a local-first, tool-governed, robust architecture. At its core is a RuleEngine-centered control layer that processes structured context, performs rule-based state transitions, and generates execution plans for typical calibration workflows. Language models are used only for natural-language interaction, high-level task understanding, and exception support, keeping the critical fast path efficient. We implement a single qubit tune-up workflow as a demonstration and validation using real quantum device dataset. We also prove that the framework achieves quantitatively acceptable levels in terms of resource cost, LLM calling times and decision latency, enabling its practical deployment in large-scale quantum qubit measurement and control scenarios. This work presents a general workflow-oriented framework for QMC and provides evidence that rule-centered architectures are a promising design choice for scalable quantum-system calibration.
tldr: This paper introduces QMClaw, a rule-engine-centered framework for scalable quantum measurement and control, using LLMs only for high-level tasks.
motivation: Existing QMC frameworks are specialized and task-specific, while LLM-based agents are too slow for large-scale quantum systems, necessitating a general-purpose, low-latency solution.
method: The framework employs a RuleEngine control layer to manage structured context and generate execution plans, reserving LLM usage for natural-language interaction and exception handling.
result: A single qubit tune-up workflow was implemented and tested on real quantum device data, showing acceptable resource cost, LLM call counts, and decision latency.
conclusion: The rule-centered architecture is presented as a promising design choice for scalable quantum-system calibration and control.

title: Decoding Error Probability Of The Random Code Ensemble Over The Erasure Channel
authors: Chin Hei Chan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide explicit formulas for the average decoding error probabilities of the ensemble of all [MATH] codes over the erasure channel under unambiguous, list and maximum-likelihood decoding principles. Moreover, we derive the asymptotic error exponents for the ensemble of all [MATH] codes.
tldr: This paper derives explicit formulas and asymptotic error exponents for decoding error probabilities of random code ensembles over the erasure channel under three different decoding principles.
motivation: To characterize the theoretical performance limits of random codes on the erasure channel, which is a fundamental problem in classical coding theory.
method: The author provides explicit mathematical derivations for average error probabilities under unambiguous, list, and maximum-likelihood decoding, and analyzes their asymptotic error exponents.
result: Exact expressions for decoding error probabilities and error exponents are obtained for the ensemble of all codes over the erasure channel.
conclusion: The paper contributes to classical information theory but has no direct connection to quantum information or quantum coding, thus low relevance to the stated research interests.

title: A Representation-Theoretic Framework For Characterizing Barren Plateaus
authors: Pedro Alc\^antara, Leandro Morais, Rafael Chaves
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scalability of variational quantum algorithms is fundamentally limited by the barren plateau effect, where the cost-function variance vanishes with system size, rendering optimization impractical. Recent Lie-algebraic approaches for deep parameterized have enabled a unified analytical understanding of this challenge but require either the initial state or the measurement observable to belong to the dynamical Lie algebra generated by the circuit. Here, we introduce a representation-theoretic framework under [MATH]-design hypothesis showing that variational quantum landscapes admit a natural decomposition into irreducible representation channels. This yields exact expressions and analytical bounds for the cost-function variance applicable to arbitrary initial states and observables, with previous Lie-algebraic results emerging as a special case. We illustrate the framework by analyzing the energy landscape of the one-dimensional ANNNI model for several circuit architectures, revealing trainability regimes inaccessible to existing methods. Our results establish a general representation-theoretic framework for analyzing variational quantum landscapes, substantially extending the analytical theory of barren plateaus.
tldr: Introduces a representation-theoretic framework to analyze barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms, providing exact cost-function variance expressions for arbitrary initial states and observables.
motivation: Barren plateaus limit the scalability of variational quantum algorithms; existing Lie-algebraic methods require the initial state or observable to be in the dynamical Lie algebra.
method: Uses representation theory and a [MATH]-design hypothesis to decompose the variational landscape into irreducible representation channels, yielding analytical variance bounds.
result: Provides exact expressions and bounds for cost-function variance applicable to arbitrary states and observables, generalizing previous Lie-algebraic results; illustrated on the 1D ANNNI model.
conclusion: Establishes a general representation-theoretic framework for analyzing variational quantum landscapes, extending the analytical theory of barren plateaus.

title: Strong-Drive Floquet Engineering Of Interacting Qudits: From Finite-Duration Controls To Emergent Symmetry
authors: V. W. Scarola Ryan Scott
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Floquet driving uses periodic controls to tailor the behavior of quantum systems, with applications in quantum analogue simulation, sensing, and the protection of quantum information. Most approaches are designed using idealized, instantaneous pulses, even though experiments necessarily use pulses with finite duration and shape. This mismatch becomes especially challenging for interacting [MATH]-level systems, or qudits, because the number of possible controls grows rapidly with the number of levels. We develop a strong-drive Floquet theory that incorporates experimentally realizable pulse waveforms directly into the design of the effective interactions. The pulse duration, amplitude, and shape therefore become useful control parameters rather than sources of error. We show that systems with more than two levels offer capabilities unavailable in qubit systems: finite-duration driving can create new interactions that are absent from the original system and can substantially change its symmetries. We demonstrate these capabilities for interacting three-level systems. A single pulse transforms a diagonal interaction into a quantum spin-1 model dominated by nematic interactions, while pulse protocols motivated by trapped ultracold polar molecules produce models with enlarged [MATH] and [MATH] symmetries. Numerical tests of both short-time evolution and many-body dynamics confirm the accuracy of the resulting description. Our results provide a scalable analytical framework for designing finite-duration controls in interacting qudit platforms.
tldr: This paper develops a strong-drive Floquet theory for interacting qudits with finite-duration pulses, enabling new effective interactions and symmetry changes in systems like spin-1 models.
motivation: Existing Floquet engineering often assumes instantaneous pulses, which is unrealistic for experiments; moreover, qudit systems offer more control possibilities but are less studied.
method: The authors incorporate experimentally realizable pulse waveforms into Floquet theory, deriving effective Hamiltonians for finite-duration driving, and demonstrate on three-level systems.
result: They show that finite-duration pulses can produce interactions (e.g., nematic) and enlarged symmetries (e.g., SU(2) and SU(3)) that are absent in qubit systems, with numerical verification.
conclusion: The framework provides a scalable analytical method for designing finite-duration controls in interacting qudit platforms, expanding the toolset for quantum simulation and information protection.

title: Phase Independent Measurement Of Weak Coherent Optical Signals
authors: Lani Chastain, Priya Drashni, Mahadeva Chanda Durjoy, Hari P. Lamsal, Girish S. Agarwal, Tian Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a quantum sensing framework for the phase independent detection of weak coherent optical displacements based on SU(1,1) interferometry. Unlike conventional quantum measurement protocols that require prior knowledge of the signal phase and coherent homodyne detection, the proposed approach estimates the displacement magnitude independently of its phase. We show that, under ideal lossless conditions, a conventional SU(1,1) interferometer employing only total intensity detection saturates the quantum Cramer Rao bound for displacement magnitude estimation. We further derive the analytical expression of the quantum Cramer Rao bound and the sensitivity of the conventional SU(1,1) interferometer with total intensity detection and systematically investigate its performance in the presence of optical loss. The proposed phase-independent intensity detection scheme achieves comparable performance over experimentally relevant operating regimes while eliminating the need for local oscillators, phase locking, and quadrature tracking. These results establish SU(1,1) based intensity detection as a practical platform for phase independent quantum sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum sensing framework using SU(1,1) interferometry for phase-independent detection of weak coherent optical displacements, achieving quantum-limited sensitivity without local oscillators or phase locking.
motivation: Conventional quantum measurement protocols require prior knowledge of signal phase and coherent homodyne detection; the authors aim to develop a technique that estimates displacement magnitude without phase information, simplifying practical implementation.
method: The authors employ a conventional SU(1,1) interferometer with total intensity detection, derive the quantum Cramér-Rao bound analytically, and analyze its sensitivity and performance under optical loss.
result: Under ideal lossless conditions, the scheme saturates the quantum Cramér-Rao bound for displacement magnitude estimation, and it exhibits comparable performance over experimentally relevant regimes even in the presence of loss.
conclusion: The proposed SU(1,1) intensity detection scheme establishes a practical platform for phase-independent quantum sensing, eliminating the need for local oscillators, phase locking, and quadrature tracking.

title: Qmes: Quantum Meta-Learning For Encoding Selection In Quantum Kernel Methods
authors: Dao Duy Tung, Quoc Chuong Nguyen, Vu Tuan Hai, Le Bin Ho, Lan Nguyen Tran
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Selecting an effective encoding quantum circuit is a key challenge in quantum kernel methods because different feature maps can lead to different performance. Conventional methods require constructing and evaluating every circuit for each new dataset, making it computationally expensive. We present Qmes, an open-source Python package that automatically recommends circuits through meta-learning. Qmes characterizes a dataset using classical complexity measures and queries a pre-trained model to recommend circuits without quantum evaluation at inference time. The package provides modular components for meta-feature extraction, quantum-kernel evaluation, recommender training, model selection, and user-defined circuit extension. We validate Qmes on 105 classification and 86 regression benchmark datasets. Qmes reduces the mean recommendation regret by 2.2x and 4.2x for classification and regression, respectively, compared to a non-adaptive baseline, with statistical significance confirmed via a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test ([MATH]). Qmes thus enables efficient and practical encoding-circuit selection for quantum kernel methods.
tldr: Qmes is an open-source Python package that uses meta-learning to recommend encoding quantum circuits for quantum kernel methods without quantum evaluation at inference time.
motivation: Selecting an effective encoding circuit for quantum kernels is costly because it requires evaluating each circuit for each new dataset. A method to automatically recommend circuits without quantum evaluation would save computational resources.
method: The package characterizes a dataset using classical complexity measures, then uses a pre-trained meta-learning model to recommend encoding circuits. It also provides modular components for meta-feature extraction, quantum-kernel evaluation, recommender training, and model selection.
result: Qmes reduces mean recommendation regret by 2.2x for classification and 4.2x for regression compared to a non-adaptive baseline, with significance confirmed via a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
conclusion: Qmes enables efficient and practical encoding-circuit selection for quantum kernel methods, avoiding exhaustive evaluations and improving performance on benchmark datasets.

title: Algebraic Geometry Codes Approach The Half-Singleton Bound With Constant Field Size
authors: Neehar Verma, Camilla Hollanti, Razane Tajeddine
abstract: ArXiv:2609.05017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study linear codes for insertion and deletion (insdel) errors through the lens of evaluation codes. We develop a general framework for analyzing random puncturings of evaluation codes, where the edit distance is controlled by only the size of the evaluation domain and the maximum number of zeros of a nonzero function in the underlying function space. Our proof generalizes the results of Con, Guo, Li, and Zhang (ICALP 2025), and simultaneously simplifies their arguments by avoiding an in-depth analysis of longest common subsequences. We demonstrate the applicability of our core theorem by instantiating it with random puncturings of Reed--Muller codes. We then recover the result that random Reed--Solomon codes approach the half-Singleton bound over linear-sized fields while also improving the dependence on the additive gap [MATH] from [MATH] to [MATH]. Finally, by applying the framework to algebraic geometry codes arising from asymptotically good towers of function fields, we show that there exist randomized families of structured linear codes over constant-sized fields that approach the half-Singleton bound.
tldr: This paper introduces a general framework for random puncturings of evaluation codes and shows that algebraic geometry codes can approach the half-Singleton bound for insertion-deletion errors with constant field size.
motivation: To construct error-correcting codes that approach the half-Singleton bound for insertion-deletion errors, a classical coding theory problem, and to do so with constant-sized fields, which is desirable for practical applications.
method: The authors develop a framework where the edit distance of random puncturings of evaluation codes is controlled by the evaluation domain size and the maximum number of zeros of a nonzero function, then instantiate it with Reed-Muller and algebraic geometry codes.
result: They prove that random Reed-Solomon codes approach the bound over linear-sized fields with improved parameters, and that there exist randomized families of algebraic geometry codes over constant-sized fields that approach the half-Singleton bound.
conclusion: The framework simplifies existing proofs and provides a systematic method to achieve near-optimal insdel codes, but the work is purely classical and does not connect to quantum information or the other research directions.

title: p-Adic Dirac Equations, Continuous-Time Quantum Walks, And Quantum Networks
authors: W. A. Z\'u\~niga-Galindo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new class of p-adic Dirac equations, formulated in the standard axiomatic framework of quantum mechanics, in which the ordinary spatial derivatives are replaced by non-local operators built from arbitrary integrable kernels. We diagonalize the resulting free Dirac Hamiltonian in momentum space, construct its plane-wave solutions, determine its spectrum, and establish a p-adic charge-conjugation symmetry relating particle and antiparticle sectors. We then discretize the free equation in two ways, both giving genuine continuous-time quantum walks rather than the discrete-time, coined walks that dominate the existing literature: a first construction on a countable covering of the underlying p-adic space, and a second, more explicit construction on a finite, tree-structured graph, for which we prove that the transition probabilities, once the internal (particle/antiparticle) components of the wavefunction are combined, form a genuine, properly normalized set of transition probabilities at every instant of time; in other words, ignoring the internal structure of the walk, it behaves exactly like an ordinary random walk on that graph. Building on this stochastic-matrix property, we discuss how the resulting construction can serve as the foundation of a quantum network with genuinely relativistic-type internal degrees of freedom, complementing earlier, non-relativistic p-adic quantum neural networks. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first continuous-time quantum walk whose free dynamics coincides exactly with a Dirac equation on a hierarchical graph. We close with a discussion of the open mathematical and computational problems raised by this construction.
tldr: Introduces a new class of p-adic Dirac equations and discretizes them into continuous-time quantum walks that behave like ordinary random walks on hierarchical graphs, proposed as a foundation for quantum networks with relativistic internal degrees of freedom.
motivation: To extend p-adic frameworks to quantum dynamics with relativistic features, building on prior non-relativistic p-adic quantum neural networks.
method: Formulates p-adic Dirac equations with non-local kernels, diagonalizes the free Hamiltonian in momentum space, and discretizes the equation into continuous-time quantum walks on both countable and finite tree-structured graphs.
result: Shows that the discretized walks yield properly normalized transition probabilities at each instant, effectively behaving as ordinary random walks when internal particle/antiparticle components are combined.
conclusion: Proposes these walks as a basis for quantum networks with relativistic-type internal degrees of freedom, while leaving open several mathematical and computational challenges.

title: Fukui-Kawakami Chains: Spectrum And Hidden $\mathfrak{gl}(1|1)$-symmetry
authors: Antoine Lefebvre Rob Klabbers
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fukui and Kawakami showed that the trigonometric Haldane--Shastry (HS) spin chain can be deformed by introducing twisted boundary conditions. In this work we revisit the resulting twisted HS chains, which we call Fukui--Kawakami (FK) chains. We analyse their spectra in dependence of the twist parameter, utilising a direct connection with the (untwisted) HS chain. This allows us to explain why part of the spectrum can be described by Fukui and Kawakami's twisted Bethe equations, and can be constructed from Yangian highest weight states. These states can be labelled by combinatorial data called `motifs', as in the HS chain, which cover some of the (deformed) descendants. We furthermore show that there are other descendants which do not follow from these Bethe equations, but whose energy can be described as a sum of two single-particle energies, suggesting additional hidden symmetries. We then focus on the special case of antiperiodic boundary conditions, and show that this chain coincides with the `minimally polarised' long-range model recently introduced by Basu-Mallick, Finkel, and Gonz\'alez-L\'opez. Remarkably, this connection implies that the antiperiodic chain has a hidden [MATH]-symmetry, which we use to relate the HS motifs to their `supersymmetric' [MATH] counterparts.
tldr: The paper analyzes the spectrum and hidden symmetries of Fukui-Kawakami chains, deformed Haldane-Shastry spin chains, revealing connections to Yangian highest weight states and a hidden gl(1|1) symmetry in the antiperiodic case.
motivation: To understand the spectral properties and symmetries of twisted Haldane-Shastry chains, and to explain why part of the spectrum can be described by twisted Bethe equations.
method: They revisit twisted HS chains, analyze spectra via connection with the untwisted HS chain, identify states that follow from Bethe equations and others with additive energy, and show the antiperiodic case has a hidden gl(1|1) symmetry.
result: They explain the spectrum structure, identify combinatorial motifs, and establish that antiperiodic chains have a hidden supersymmetric symmetry relating HS motifs to their super counterparts.
conclusion: The work reveals additional hidden symmetries and connections between long-range integrable models.

title: Toward Resilient Many-Body Formulations Under Incomplete Correlation Models: A Dual-Space Variational Formulation
authors: Vibin Abraham, Bhumika Jayee, Bo Peng, Nicholas P. Bauman, Karol Kowalski
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum simulations of correlated many-body systems will inevitably operate with imperfect information: the prepared states may arise from incomplete or approximate ansatze, while their measured Hamiltonian and overlap matrix elements are additionally affected by hardware and statistical noise. Robust quantum algorithms will be those that can improve upon reliable lower-level descriptions in spite of these imperfections. We introduce a dual-space nonorthogonal configuration-interaction (DS-NOCI) framework built around this principle. Rather than replacing a classically accessible NOCI reference manifold with correlated quantum states, DS-NOCI retains both spaces and couples them variationally. The reference sector provides a stable many-body backbone, while the quantum states contribute whatever additional correlation directions they contain. With exact matrix elements, the enlarged dual space gives a ground-state energy no higher than either the reference-only NOCI or correlated-only quantum-NOCI spaces, ensuring that an incomplete correlation model cannot degrade the underlying variational description. The additional reference--correlated matrix elements require only one correlated state preparation and are therefore less demanding than the correlated--correlated block already required by quantum variant of NOCI. Molecular benchmarks further show enhanced resilience to imperfect amplitudes and noisy matrix elements. DS-NOCI thus provides a general strategy for building quantum many-body formulations that remain useful when both correlation models and quantum computations are necessarily incomplete and noisy.
tldr: This paper introduces a dual-space nonorthogonal configuration-interaction (DS-NOCI) method that couples classical reference states with correlated quantum states to improve robustness of quantum many-body simulations against noise and incomplete models.
motivation: Quantum simulations of correlated many-body systems are often based on incomplete or noisy information, so robust algorithms are needed that can still improve upon reliable lower-level descriptions despite these imperfections.
method: DS-NOCI retains both a classically accessible NOCI reference manifold and a set of correlated quantum states, coupling them variationally in an enlarged dual space to ensure that the resulting ground-state energy is no higher than that of either the reference-only or correlated-only NOCI.
result: With exact matrix elements, DS-NOCI guarantees a ground-state energy lower than or equal to its components, and molecular benchmarks demonstrate enhanced resilience to imperfect amplitudes and noisy matrix elements.
conclusion: DS-NOCI offers a general, robust strategy for quantum many-body simulations that remain useful even when correlation models and quantum computations are incomplete and noisy.

title: Gradient-based Optimal Control Of The non-Hermitian Skin Effect In Optomechanical Arrays
authors: Juste Deuyekbe, Philippe Djorw\'e, A. -H. Abdel-Aty, A. Elrashidi, Nsangou Mama, Serge Guy Nana Engo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In single-port non-Hermitian sensors the Petermann factor offsets susceptibility gains, imposing a strict resource bound on metrological precision. We test whether a multi-port geometry can evade this bound: a double-chain optomechanical ladder with opposing non-reciprocal hoppings spatially separates signal amplification from quantum-noise drainage, and gradient-based differentiable optimal control (DOC) maximizes the resource-normalized Fisher information [MATH] subject to a Hurwitz-stability constraint. Across system sizes [MATH] the optimizer returns [MATH] in every case, with two coexisting solution classes whose selection is initialization-dependent: deep-stability configurations achieve [MATH] with attenuated transmission, while marginal-stability configurations deliver directional gain [MATH] with isolation [MATH]. A multi-restart ensemble reveals these classes are the endpoints of a precision--gain frontier. All solutions remain Hurwitz-stable under {\percent} disorder ({\percent} recovery), and the deep-stability advantage survives realistic preamplifier noise at [MATH]--[MATH]. Mapped onto circuit-QED parameters, the architecture enables sub-attonewton force sensing and broadband axion searches across the {10}{\giga\hertz} band.
tldr: The paper proposes gradient-based optimal control for non-Hermitian optomechanical arrays to enhance sensing precision, demonstrating a two-class solution frontier that outperforms single-port limits.
motivation: Single-port non-Hermitian sensors face a fundamental precision bound due to the Petermann factor; a multi-port geometry could circumvent this by separating amplification and noise drainage.
method: They model a double-chain optomechanical ladder with opposing non-reciprocal hoppings and apply differentiable optimal control to maximize Fisher information under stability constraints, using multi-restart ensembles to explore solution classes.
result: The optimizer consistently achieves a fixed value across system sizes, with deep-stability and marginal-stability solutions forming a precision-gain frontier; all solutions remain stable under disorder and realistic noise.
conclusion: The architecture, when mapped to circuit-QED parameters, enables sub-attonewton force sensing and broadband axion searches, suggesting a new pathway for high-precision metrology.

title: X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Of Ar And Kr Clusters Formed In He Nanodroplets
authors: N. S. Blaj, N. Scheel, R. Rajni, A. {\O}. L{\ae}gdsmand, J. Sadasivan, S. De, S. R. Krishnan, J. Bozek, A. R. Milosavljevi\'c, M. Mudrich
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the first soft x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements of Ar and Kr clusters formed inside superfluid helium nanodroplets (HNDs) through consecutive pickup of dopant atoms. Ar and Kr atoms and clusters are selectively inner-shell ionized (Ar 2p, Kr 3d) using monochromatic soft x-ray synchrotron radiation. In the regime of strong doping, the electron spectra exhibit features characteristic of free Ar and Kr atoms as well as their clusters. The Kr cluster spectra agree well with literature data for bare Kr clusters. Backed by detailed simulations of the pickup process, this agreement indicates that the observed spectra originate from nearly bare Ar and Kr clusters, from which most or all He has evaporated in the course of cluster aggregation. These results establish HNDs as a platform for XPS of various types of molecular complexes and nanostructures.
tldr: First soft X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy of Ar and Kr clusters formed in helium nanodroplets, showing spectra from nearly bare clusters after helium evaporation.
motivation: To explore helium nanodroplets as a platform for XPS of molecular complexes and nanostructures, and to understand cluster formation dynamics.
method: Inner-shell ionization of Ar and Kr dopants in superfluid helium nanodroplets using monochromatic soft X-ray synchrotron radiation, combined with pickup simulations.
result: Observed cluster spectra match literature for bare clusters, indicating most helium evaporates during aggregation.
conclusion: Helium nanodroplets can be used for XPS studies of dopant clusters and complexes, extending their utility in nanoscience.

title: Band Gaps And Localization Of Surface Waves At Hyperbolic Material And Topological Insulator Interfaces
authors: Andrei I. Maimistov, Ildar R. Gabitov, Ilia Kuk
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop analytical criteria for surface electromagnetic waves at interfaces between hyperbolic materials and topological insulators. The analysis identifies propagation conditions, field penetration depths, and spectral band gaps. In the lossless model, the band edge is governed primarily by dielectric contrast, while the bulk topological coupling produces only a small shift and a weak correction to the dispersion. For structures combining hexagonal boron nitride with bismuth selenide, a thin topological insulator film on a dielectric substrate with low permittivity can substantially broaden the accessible propagation window. We also analyze a dissipative titanium and silicon hyperbolic effective medium interfaced with bismuth selenide. To make the complex branch structure visible, this lossy calculation uses an intentionally enhanced interface response and is therefore illustrative rather than a quantitative prediction for a conventional topological insulator. In the lossy case, a root of the dispersion relation represents a physical guided mode only when the fields decay away from the interface, attenuate consistently along the propagation direction, have finite penetration depths, and exhibit a consistent energy flow profile. Apparent gaps and jumps can occur when the complex quantities controlling transverse decay approach square root branch cuts. These results provide design guidelines for controlling dispersion, confinement, band gaps, and propagation loss in mid-infrared photonic structures.
tldr: The paper develops analytical criteria for surface electromagnetic waves at hyperbolic material and topological insulator interfaces, analyzing band gaps, penetration depths, and dispersion in lossless and lossy cases.
motivation: To provide design guidelines for controlling dispersion, confinement, band gaps, and propagation loss in mid-infrared photonic structures using hyperbolic materials and topological insulators.
method: The authors derive analytical conditions for surface wave propagation at interfaces, considering dielectric contrast and bulk topological coupling, and analyze specific material combinations such as hBN with Bi2Se3 and a dissipative Ti/Si hyperbolic medium.
result: In lossless case, band edges are governed mainly by dielectric contrast; a thin topological insulator film on a low-permittivity substrate broadens the propagation window. In lossy case, only roots with decaying fields and consistent energy flow represent physical guided modes.
conclusion: The results offer practical guidelines for engineering surface waves in mid-infrared photonic structures, though the lossy analysis is illustrative rather than quantitatively predictive for conventional topological insulators.

title: Research And Simulation Of Analytical Polarization Control Enabled By Optical Computing On An Integrated Photonics Chip
authors: Xueying Ren, Junxin Yan, Xuyang Wang, Bailin Shen, Lingyan Zhang, Minyue Yang, Nannan Ning, Jiaxin Huang, Zhenguo Lu, Jun Zou, Yongmin Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic polarization controllers are key devices with broad applications in many fields. However, most on-chip polarization controllers still rely on traditional blind-search methods, whereas analytical optical-computing approaches remain insufficiently explored, particularly with respect to calibration and endless polarization control. With the accurate relative phase of Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) being fully controllable on an integrated photonics chip, we present an analytical polarization control (APC) method using four phase shifters and optical computing, eliminating the need for the traditional inefficient blind-search procedure. The basic structures and operations of APC are clarified. The proposed calibration method and endless control method enable continuous APC while compensating for phase differences within the MZI structures. We simulate the influence of the endless control unit on polarization control and quantify the effect of the fourth phase difference on the output extinction ratio. With the fourth phase shifter, the phase difference encountered during Stokes vector measurement can be effectively compensated, and rotations around all three axes on the Poincar\'e sphere can be realized. These results establish a practical APC architecture based on optical computing for photonics chips. The proposed APC methods, combined with a FPGA-based hardware acceleration, will enable high speed on-chip polarization controllers.
tldr: This paper presents an analytical polarization control method using optical computing on an integrated photonics chip, eliminating blind-search procedures.
motivation: Traditional on-chip polarization controllers rely on inefficient blind-search methods, and analytical approaches are insufficiently explored, particularly for calibration and endless control.
method: The proposed APC method uses four phase shifters and optical computing, with MZI structures, including calibration and endless control methods to compensate phase differences.
result: Simulations show that with the fourth phase shifter, phase differences can be compensated and rotations around all three axes on the Poincaré sphere can be realized.
conclusion: The architecture enables high-speed on-chip polarization controllers, potentially combined with FPGA-based hardware acceleration.

title: Breakdown Of The Overdamped Approximation In Fluctuating Environments
authors: Takuma Akimoto Kazuki Fukutani
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The overdamped approximation is widely used to describe Brownian motion in complex environments, but its validity becomes nontrivial when the friction coefficient itself fluctuates in time. We investigate this problem by comparing underdamped and overdamped Langevin dynamics subject to the same fluctuating friction and satisfying the fluctuation--dissipation relation at a common temperature. We show that environmental averaging and inertial elimination generally lead to different long-time transport when environmental fluctuations are fast compared with velocity relaxation. For rapidly fluctuating friction, the underdamped dynamics is governed by the arithmetic mean friction and yields [MATH], whereas the overdamped dynamics gives [MATH]. For a two-state Markov friction, we derive the finite-time effective diffusion coefficient exactly and identify the full crossover between these two regimes, controlled by the competition between velocity relaxation and environmental switching. We further establish the fast-fluctuation result for general stationary friction processes and verify it for a continuous log-Ornstein--Uhlenbeck environment, for which the characteristic crossover time can also be determined independently. Our results reveal a noncommutativity between environmental averaging and inertial elimination, establish a timescale-dependent criterion for the validity of overdamped dynamics in temporally heterogeneous environments, and show that rapid environmental fluctuations can enhance, rather than suppress, the consequences of inertia.
tags: non-commutativity of averaging and inertial elimination
tldr: The paper shows that when friction fluctuates rapidly compared to velocity relaxation, the overdamped approximation yields incorrect long-time transport, revealing a noncommutativity between environmental averaging and inertial elimination.
motivation: To investigate the validity of the overdamped approximation when the friction coefficient fluctuates in time, as in complex environments.
method: Compare underdamped and overdamped Langevin dynamics with identical fluctuating friction and fluctuation-dissipation relation; derive exact effective diffusion coefficients for two-state Markov friction and general stationary processes.
result: Under rapid friction fluctuations, underdamped dynamics gives arithmetic mean friction, while overdamped gives a different result; fast fluctuations can enhance consequences of inertia; a timescale-dependent criterion for overdamped validity is established.
conclusion: The overdamped approximation breaks down when environmental fluctuations are fast relative to velocity relaxation; there's a noncommutativity between averaging and inertial elimination.
keywords: non-commutativity of averaging and inertial elimination

title: Analytical Model For Polarization Transfer During Gas-phase Collision Events In Spin-exchange Optical Pumping: Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ $^{129}$Xe Versus Spin-$\frac{3}{2}$ $^{131}$Xe
authors: Perttu Hilla, Rajgowrav Cheenikundil, Juha Vaara
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin-exchange optical pumping (SEOP) is a method for producing spin-hyperpolarized noble gas nuclei, such as 129Xe and 131Xe, which are used in various magnetic resonance applications from fundamental physics to quantum sensing and medical imaging. In SEOP, optically polarized alkali-metal atoms transfer their spin polarization to the noble gas nuclei in gas-phase collision events via the hyperfine coupling (HFC) between the alkali valence electron and the noble gas nucleus. While the polarization transfer physics of spin [MATH] nuclei, such as 129Xe, is relatively well understood, that of spin [MATH] nuclei, such as 131Xe ([MATH]), has been far less studied, and no rigorous theoretical model has been presented to date. To this end, we derive a simple analytical model for the upper limit, neglecting relaxation, of the SEOP polarization transfer, applicable to noble gases with arbitrary nuclear spin. Analytical evaluation of the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion for the time evolution of the spin density operator [MATH] reveals that only even-order terms in the HFC contribute to the polarization transfer, with the leading-order quadratic term being the most significant. We obtain a result similar to that derived for the spin-exchange cross section by Herman [Phys. Rev. 137, A 1062 (1965)], but in a more general framework for the time evolution of [MATH] that is also more familiar to magnetic resonance researchers. The model is applied to understand the difference in the polarization transfer efficiency between 129Xe and 131Xe, yielding results in agreement with previous experiments. We also validate the model by comparison to detailed numerical multiscale simulations of the SEOP process, where full quantum-chemically computed spin Hamiltonians sampled from molecular dynamics simulations of the gas-phase collision events are used to propagate the spin dynamics.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical model for spin-exchange optical pumping polarization transfer to noble gas nuclei with arbitrary spin, explaining efficiency differences between spin-1/2 129Xe and spin-3/2 131Xe.
motivation: To provide a rigorous theoretical model for polarization transfer to spin-3/2 noble gases like 131Xe, which has been less studied than spin-1/2 nuclei, and to understand the efficiency difference.
method: Derivation of an analytical model for the upper limit of polarization transfer neglecting relaxation, using analytical evaluation of the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion for the time evolution of the spin density operator, showing only even-order terms in hyperfine coupling contribute.
result: The model yields results consistent with previous experiments and numerical multiscale simulations, explaining the lower polarization efficiency for 131Xe compared to 129Xe.
conclusion: The analytical model provides a simple framework applicable to noble gases with arbitrary nuclear spin and clarifies the physics of polarization transfer in SEOP.

title: Shapley Valuation Of Finite-Copy Quantum Data Depends On Physical Access
authors: Yuntao Qian Qipeng Qian
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data valuation asks how learning utility should be attributed to training data contributors. Most classical formulations begin after data have become reusable records, so the physical readout of the data is effectively fixed. Finite-copy quantum data are different: unknown states are consumable physical systems, and the same supplied states and downstream task can yield different Shapley values under different physical access models. Our framework makes this dependence explicit by treating physical access as a component of quantum data valuation itself. We establish an exact connection between physical-access advantage and contributor-level data valuation. For nested access models, we prove that the maximal downstream utility gain enabled by richer physical access exactly determines the largest symmetric Shapley ranking-reversal margin. More generally, for arbitrary access-model pairs, including non-nested ones, we derive an exact geometric characterization of the possible shifts of the full Shapley attribution vector. For fixed learning pipelines, we further obtain an operational Shapley-observable representation for finite-copy valuation. Numerical experiments demonstrate that identical quantum samples can receive different values and rankings when only the physical access model is changed. These results establish that quantum data value is not an intrinsic property of the underlying states alone, but emerges from the interaction between quantum states, physical access, and the downstream learning task.
tldr: This paper shows that Shapley values for quantum data depend on physical access models, indicating that quantum data value is not intrinsic but emerges from the interaction between states, access, and task.
motivation: To understand how to attribute utility to quantum data contributors, considering that quantum states are consumable and physical access models affect the valuation.
method: The authors formulate a framework with physical access as a component of quantum data valuation, and derive theoretical results including exact connections between access advantage and Shapley ranking margins, geometric characterizations for arbitrary access models, and operational representations for fixed learning pipelines.
result: They prove that maximal downstream utility gain from richer physical access determines the largest Shapley ranking-reversal margin, and provide an operational Shapley-observable representation; numerical experiments confirm that different access models lead to different values and rankings.
conclusion: Quantum data value is not intrinsic to the states but depends on physical access and the downstream task, providing a new perspective on data valuation in quantum settings.

title: Derived Associative Algebras And Cyclic Cohomology Of Q-manifolds
authors: Andrew James Bruce
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Loday's derived product is revisited in the setting of Q-manifolds, i.e., supermanifolds equipped with an odd vector field that `squares to zero'. We interpret the Grassmann odd product as a standard product upon shifting the grading, which implies the existence of a derived (noncommutative) associative [MATH]-graded algebra associated with any Q-manifold. We apply Connes' cyclic cohomology to the derived associative algebra, giving a new cohomology on Q-manifolds distinct from the standard cohomology: we refer to this as the derived cyclic cohomology of a Q-manifold. The derived cyclic cocycles are interpreted as classically BRST-invariant functionals within the BV--BFV--BRST formalism or generalised Ruelle--Sullivan currents when applied to regular foliations via their foliation Lie algebroids.
tldr: This paper introduces derived associative algebras and a new cyclic cohomology for Q-manifolds, connecting to BRST formalism and foliation Lie algebroids.
motivation: The work aims to reinterpret Loday's derived product on Q-manifolds and apply Connes' cyclic cohomology to derive a new cohomology theory distinct from standard cohomology.
method: The author shifts grading to interpret the Grassmann odd product as a standard product, constructs a derived associative graded algebra, and applies cyclic cohomology to define derived cyclic cohomology on Q-manifolds.
result: The derived cyclic cocycles are interpreted as classically BRST-invariant functionals within the BV–BFV–BRST formalism or as generalized Ruelle–Sullivan currents for regular foliations via foliation Lie algebroids.
conclusion: This introduces a novel cohomology for Q-manifolds that may have applications in mathematical physics and noncommutative geometry, but it is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dead-zone-free Free-induction-decay Alkali-metal Atomic Magnetometer
authors: X. -K. Wang, J. He, H. -H. Deng, W. Gao, D. Sheng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detection dead zone is an important systematic limitation in scalar atomic magnetometers, constraining their practical utility. In this work, we demonstrate a sensitive dead zone free scalar magnetometer by integrating previously established techniques into a FID magnetometer based on Bell Bloom optical pumping. The dead zone is eliminated by inserting a reflecting mirror within a multipass cavity assisted atomic cell, which folds the optical beam into orthogonal paths. Our analysis reveals that interregion cross talk is essential for interpreting the resulted experimental signals. The sensor exhibits oscillation signal amplitude variations within a factor of three across all orientations in three dimensional space, and a field sensitivity better than 80 fT/Hz^(1/2) over the full space. We further characterize the heading error in the geomagnetic field range, where experimental results agree with theoretical predictions within 0.7 nT. Additionally, the sensor can operate in a closed loop mode by feeding back the real time frequency extracted from the FID signal to modulate the pump beam, we characterize the magnetic field slew rate of the sensor. This work paves the way towards a sensitive vector FID magnetometer.
tldr: This paper presents a dead-zone-free scalar atomic magnetometer using free-induction decay with Bell-Bloom optical pumping, achieving high sensitivity across all orientations.
motivation: To overcome the detection dead zone limitation in scalar atomic magnetometers, which restricts their practical use.
method: Integrates a reflecting mirror in a multipass cavity assisted atomic cell to fold the optical beam into orthogonal paths, and analyzes interregion cross talk.
result: Achieves oscillation signal variations within a factor of three across all orientations and field sensitivity better than 80 fT/Hz^(1/2) over full space, with heading error agreement within 0.7 nT.
conclusion: Paves the way towards a sensitive vector FID magnetometer.

title: Microkelvin Resolution Thermometry At The Nanometre Scale
authors: Jack W. Hart, Soham Pal, Julien R. E. Roth, Katie Ninham, Abbie H. Aleksandrova, Xander Peetroons, Soumen Mandal, Oliver A. Williams, Gavin W. Morley, Mete Atature, Helena S. Knowles
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate temperature readings of transient events at the nanometer scale are challenging due to the low sensitivity of available sensors. Nanodiamonds containing nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers have been used for nanoscale thermometry in complex environments, including inside living cells. However, their performance has been limited by short coherence times and low photon counts. In this work, we use isotopically-purified dual-NV nanodiamonds and a bespoke quantum sensing chip to showcase an order of magnitude improvement in temperature measurement sensitivity compared with previous reports. We demonstrate robust temperature measurements with an error of 682 [MATH]K, experimental sensitivities below 50 mK/[MATH] and a shot-noise limited sensitivity of 9.6 mK/[MATH]. To confirm the utility of these high-performance nanothermometers, we quantify the temperature change induced by the thermometry measurement itself, specifically the optical excitation laser used to probe the NV spin state. In addition, we observe directly at the nanometre scale the transient heating caused by the exothermic mixing of dimethyl sulfoxide in water. Sub-millikelvin resolution and millikelvin sensitivity thermometry unlock the possibility of monitoring minute thermal fluctuations in living systems and assessing catalyst performance at the nanometre scale.
tldr: The paper presents a nanoscale thermometry platform using isotopically-purified NV nanodiamonds, achieving sub-millikelvin resolution and high sensitivity for measuring temperature changes at the nanometre scale.
motivation: Accurate temperature readings of transient events at the nanometre scale are challenging; existing NV-based sensors have limited performance due to short coherence times and low photon counts.
method: The authors used isotopically-purified dual-NV nanodiamonds and a custom quantum sensing chip to perform optical measurements of NV spin states, achieving improved sensitivity and resolution.
result: They demonstrated an order of magnitude improvement in temperature measurement sensitivity, with experimental sensitivities below 50 mK/√Hz and shot-noise limited sensitivity of 9.6 mK/√Hz, and observed transient heating effects.
conclusion: These high-performance nanothermometers can monitor minute thermal fluctuations in living systems and assess catalyst performance at the nanometre scale.

title: Loss Of Memory In The Periodic Ehrenfest Model With Small Polyhedral Scatterers
authors: Jens Marklof Christopher Lutsko
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Boltzmann--Grad limit of the Ehrenfest ``wind-tree'' model with a periodic configuration of polyhedral scatterers. The central result is a loss-of-memory effect in dimension [MATH] for a generic choice of polyhedron. This yields a Markovian limiting transport process on an extended state space and a generalised linear Boltzmann equation for the time evolution of the particle density.
tldr: This paper rigorously derives a Markovian transport limit (generalized linear Boltzmann equation) for the periodic Ehrenfest wind-tree model with polyhedral scatterers.
motivation: To understand the loss-of-memory effect and the emergence of Markovian dynamics in deterministic periodic Lorentz gases, which is a central question in kinetic theory and dynamical systems.
method: The authors analyze the Boltzmann–Grad limit of the wind-tree model with periodic polyhedral scatterers, using techniques from dynamical systems and geometry to prove the loss of memory and establish a Markovian limit process.
result: They show that in dimension d, for a generic choice of polyhedron, the particle dynamics in the scaling limit loses memory and is described by a Markovian transport process on an extended state space, leading to a generalized linear Boltzmann equation for the density.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for the kinetic description of periodic scatterers, confirming that deterministic chaos can give rise to diffusive behavior under proper scaling.

title: Generalized Upper Principal Part Of Real Planar Polynomial Vector Fields
authors: Tha\'is Maria Dalbelo, Regilene Oliveira, Otavio Henrique Perez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this paper is to generalize recent results about the topological classification of the dynamics of a real planar polynomial vector field near infinity. Given a polynomial vector field [MATH], using Newton polyhedra one can define its generalized upper principal part [MATH]. By dropping some monomials of [MATH], we define its minimal generalized upper principal part [MATH]. We prove that there exist an open and dense set [MATH] in the set of polynomial vector fields with Newton degenerate upper principal part satisfying the following property: if [MATH], then [MATH] and [MATH] are topologically equivalent near infinity, provided that [MATH] satisfies some additional non-degeneracy assumptions. Our techniques rely on toric compactification and the Normal Form Theorem.
tldr: This paper generalizes results on the topological classification of real planar polynomial vector fields near infinity by introducing the concept of a minimal generalized upper principal part and proving topological equivalence under certain non-degeneracy conditions.
motivation: The authors aim to extend known results about the topological behavior of polynomial vector fields near infinity to a broader class that includes Newton degenerate cases.
method: The approach uses Newton polyhedra to define the generalized and minimal generalized upper principal parts, and relies on toric compactification and a Normal Form Theorem to establish the equivalence.
result: It is proven that for an open and dense set of polynomial vector fields with Newton degenerate upper principal part, the vector field and its minimal generalized upper principal part are topologically equivalent near infinity, provided additional non-degeneracy assumptions hold.
conclusion: The results contribute to the qualitative theory of planar polynomial vector fields by providing a topological classification near infinity that covers a wide range of degenerate cases.

title: Multi-Principal Competition For An Exclusive Agent: Characterization And Approximation Of Nash Equilibria
authors: Luis Brice\~no-Arias, Nicol\'as Hern\'andez-Santib\'a\~nez, Vicente Moreno-Garrido
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces and studies a Principal-Agent competition model where two risk-neutral Principals compete to hire a single Agent. In this framework, the Agent chooses to work exclusively for one Principal, making the Agent's reservation utility endogenous as it is directly tied to the competing offers. We characterize the Nash equilibria of the resulting game by linking them to the individual Principal-Agent contracting problems and analyzing the Agent's selection bias. Furthermore, we introduce a numerical algorithm based on the bisection method to approximate the Nash equilibria by locating the sign changes of the Principals' value functions. The procedure is illustrated through several examples involving exponential, logarithmic, and constant relative risk aversion (CRRA) utility functions within the polynomial framework of Renner and Schmedders (2015).
tldr: This paper studies a principal-agent competition model where two principals compete to hire an exclusive agent, characterizing Nash equilibria and proposing a numerical algorithm.
motivation: The authors aim to analyze strategic contracting when an agent's outside option is endogenously determined by competing offers.
method: They characterize Nash equilibria by relating them to individual contracting problems and introduce a bisection-based algorithm to approximate equilibria via sign changes in value functions.
result: The algorithm is illustrated with exponential, logarithmic, and CRRA utility examples within the Renner-Schmedders polynomial framework.
conclusion: The paper contributes to economic contracting theory but has no connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ultra-High Resolution Method For Multipath Within A Co-Delay-Doppler Bin In Dft-p-ocdm
authors: Mingxuan Han, Weile Zhang, Feifei Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Communication systems can reuse their transmitted signals for sensing without dedicated radar transmissions. For an established DFT-preprocessed orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (DFT-P-OCDM) waveform, this task becomes difficult when several physical paths in a doubly selective channel fall into the same co-delay-Doppler bin. In this case, the number of resolvable delay classes inferred from the pilot may be smaller than the number of physical paths within the co-bin. This mismatch increases the difficulty of path number determination, fractional Doppler offset estimation, and channel reconstruction. We derive a pointwise relationship between the input and output in the DFT preprocessed Fresnel (DPF) domain for doubly selective channels with multiple paths within the co-delay-Doppler bin. Based on this input and output relation, we propose the two stage ultra high resolution (TSUR) framework. The first stage uses pilots of the phase progression to estimate delay, while the second stage uses the leakage samples to estimate the Doppler and the number of paths within each delay class. Furthermore, we derive CRLBs and analyze how the pilot configuration trades sensing resolution and communication recovery. Simulation results demonstrate that TSUR resolves same delay paths within a co-delay-Doppler bin, remains robust to exist delay offsets, and achieves lower fractional Doppler estimation errors than sequential extraction and off-grid baselines.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for high-resolution multipath estimation in DFT-P-OCDM systems, but it belongs to wireless communication and not quantum information.
motivation: To resolve multiple physical paths within a co-delay-Doppler bin in DFT-P-OCDM integrated sensing and communication.
method: Derives an input-output relationship in the DPF domain and proposes a two-stage framework (TSUR) to estimate delays, Dopplers, and path numbers.
result: Simulations show TSUR resolves same-delay paths and achieves lower Doppler estimation errors than baselines.
conclusion: The work advances signal processing for integrated sensing and communication but is outside the scope of the specified research interests.

title: Energy-Consistent Splitting And Decomposition Approaches For Coupled port-Hamiltonian ODEs
authors: Marius M\"onch, Nicole Marheineke, Andreas Bartel, Kevin Sch\"afers, Michael G\"unther
abstract: ArXiv:2609.04884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operator splitting provides an attractive approach for the numerical integration of (coupled) port-Hamiltonian systems, as it allows the underlying system structure to be exploited at the level of the individual subproblems. However, the choice of the decomposition is not unique and may strongly affect both the computational efficiency and the preservation of the energy behavior of the original system. In this work, we investigate this interplay systematically and introduce energy consistency as a criterion for assessing splitting methods for port-Hamiltonian ordinary differential equations.
